introduction.summary: The study examined how taxonomic and functional alpha diversity changed with elevation, whether species composition varied between elevational bands within the same transect, and whether taxonomic and functional beta diversity were driven by turnover or nestedness across three elevational transects in Yunnan Province.

methods.summary: This study measured five morphological traits (Weber’s length, relative eye length, relative scape length, relative mandible length, and relative hindleg length) and other measurements (head length, width, eye width, and pronotum width) on worker ants to be used for functional diversity analyses. The study measured functional alpha and beta diversity, as well as species richness, for ant communities across different sampling locations.

discussion.summary: The study measured ant species richness and functional diversity indices across three transects in different regions, observing patterns related to elevation and latitude.
